text: Brent crude jumps more than $3 after new tanker attacks. Oil prices are in the news after Brent crude settled more than $3 higher on Thursday, Nov. 5, following new attacks on tankers. The jump followed a sharp drop the day before, when oil fell to its lowest level since late August.. Oil prices have been driven by the US-Israeli war with Iran, which the United States and Israel began in February. The conflict has pushed fuel costs higher, and high gas prices were a major concern for voters in the midterm elections on Tuesday. Democrats won control of both houses of Congress in those elections, and the new Congress takes office in January. Shipping in the Gulf remains under threat. The UK maritime security agency UKMTO reported at least five vessels were hit since Sunday, a pace close to a record, and similar to October, when 35 vessels were hit, the most in any month of the war. Analysts warn that Iran's stance in negotiations with Washington is unchanged, and some expect a renewed US strike on Iran, while others see room for diplomacy.

What is Brent crude?. Brent crude is a grade of crude oil that is extracted from the North Sea. Its price serves as a worldwide benchmark for oil. In the latest session, Brent settled at $116.72 a barrel, its highest settle since April.. The Dow fell more than 600 points on Friday as oil topped $100 a barrel, and Brent closed at its highest level since April. Renewed concern over the U.S.-Iran conflict drove the rise.. Brent crude is a type of crude oil, the unrefined petroleum that is turned into fuels such as gasoline and diesel. It is named for a North Sea oilfield and is traded in futures markets. Because many oil-producing countries sell their crude at prices tied to Brent, its price is widely watched as a global reference point. Traders also follow the West Texas Intermediate grade, the main U.S. Benchmark, which trades at a different price. Brent is quoted in U.S. Dollars per barrel. A barrel is a unit of 42 U.S. Gallons. Futures contracts let buyers and sellers agree on a price today for oil delivered later. Prices move with supply, demand, and worries about conflict or disruption in oil-producing regions. On Friday, Brent rose 3.1 percent to end at $116.72. West Texas Intermediate settled at $103.27 a barrel, up 3.8 percent. The increase followed reports that the United States and Israel might be preparing renewed strikes on Iran, part of a regional war that began in late February. Traders feared the U.S.-Iran conflict could flare up again. The rise in oil added to pressure on stocks that day, when the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.23 percent, to 52,215.16, and the S&P 500 slipped 0.52 percent. Higher fuel costs also weighed on some businesses, such as discount retailers, whose profits are sensitive to diesel prices.
